lead: Massachusetts plumbing deals with very old housing, cold winters and strict septic rules. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers from Boston to the Berkshires.
risk: frozen pipes, aging pipes in old homes and septic upgrades
risk_short: frozen pipes, old pipes and septic
why: Massachusetts has some of the oldest housing in the country. Triple-deckers and older homes in Boston, Worcester and Springfield often have galvanized supply lines, cast-iron stacks and lead or old service lines.

Cold winters freeze pipes on outside walls and in basements. Outside sewered areas, Title 5 rules require septic systems to be inspected when a home is sold, and failed systems must be upgraded. The Board of State Examiners of Plumbers and Gas Fitters licenses plumbers.
tips: Insulate basement and wall pipes before winter.
Ask your utility about your service line material.
Plan for Title 5 inspection before selling a home on septic.
Have stacks in older multi-family homes inspected.
areas: Calls come from Boston and Greater Boston, Worcester, Springfield, Lowell, Cambridge, the South Shore, Cape Cod and the Berkshires.

faq.a: The Board of State Examiners of Plumbers and Gas Fitters licenses plumbers and gas fitters. Local plumbing inspectors issue permits and inspect the work.
